reels.caption:
Akasaka Tower Residence — what wealth looks like in Tokyo.

Comment "listing" to receive more information

Most "luxury" apartments in Tokyo still sit around 60–80m², with standard layouts and interiors you've seen a hundred times.

This is different.

At ¥740,000,000 (~$5M), this isn't just about buying an apartment — this is about buying into one of the most stable, high-demand segments of Tokyo real estate.

Located in Akasaka 2-chome, right in the center of Tokyo, where high earners, executives, and long-term expats actually choose to live — not just visit.

Just 4 minutes to Akasaka Station, meaning your daily life stays efficient, connected, and central.

Then the unit itself shifts everything.

102m² — significantly larger than most 2LDKs in Tokyo
30th floor corner unit — limited positioning with open skyline views
Tokyo Skytree visible on clear days — unobstructed city panorama

Fully renovated with custom finishes — not the typical plain Tokyo interior.
This doesn't feel like a standard unit, because it isn't one.

And the building matches the level.

Developed and managed by Mori Building — one of Tokyo's top-tier operators
24h concierge service
Sky lounge + terrace on the 44th floor
Guest suites, bar lounge, library, and relaxation spaces

521-unit large-scale residence — strong long-term demand and liquidity
Renovated building (2023) — maintaining premium condition
Freehold ownership — actual land ownership in central Tokyo

This is why properties like this hold value.

It's not one thing — it's size, floor, location, management, and rarity all combined in one unit.

In Tokyo, that combination doesn't show up often.

Price: ¥740,000,000 | ~$5M
Layout: 2LDK
Size: 102m² | 1097ft²

Comment "listing" to get full details and availability.
